chunks: the most prominent of the commanders of your army in your estimation to be one who assists them in his aid, and excels them from his wealth with what suffices them, and what suffices them suffices those behind them from the replacements of their families, until their concern becomes a single concern in fighting the enemy, for indeed your kindness to them will turn their hearts to you.
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim governor select and treat his military commanders according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this foundational directive from his famous letter to Malik al-Ashtar, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) emphasizes that a leader’s personal generosity and equitable distribution of resources to soldiers and their families are essential for maintaining unity of purpose in jihad. This practical application of *adl* (justice) and *ihsan* (benevolence) ensures that the troops' hearts remain attached to the commander, reflecting the Shia ideal of leadership rooted in service rather than mere authority.

en.sayed-ali-raza: That commander of the army should have such a position before you that he renders help to them equitably and spends from his money on them and on those of their families who remain behind so that all their worries converge on the one worry for fighting the enemy.
Your kindness to them will turn their hearts to you.
